# requireObject

<link-summary>Returns the value as an object, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireObject() — Returns the value as an object, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireObject(value: unknown, message: string = "Expected an object."): object;
```

The test is `typeof value === "object"` with `null` excluded, so arrays, dates and class instances all count, while a function does not. `isObjectLike` is the one that also accepts functions.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                        | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :----------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                          | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected an object."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`object` — the same value, typed as an object.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                   |
| :------------------------- | :-------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not an object. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireObject({}); // => {}
requireObject([]); // => []
requireObject(null); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireObject("abc"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
